official_sources: National Framework for Water Resources 2025 introduction
How to form and maintain a DWMP

official_measurement_examples.name: WRMP current guideline
official_measurement_examples.fact: The water resources planning guideline was updated 16 June 2026 and requires water companies to maintain long-term statutory WRMPs; it is strategic supply-demand planning rather than a parcel connection offer.

official_measurement_examples.name: WRMP29 transition
official_measurement_examples.fact: The current guideline sets a future WRMP29 timetable through 2027-2029, so future resource options must not be treated as already delivered capacity in 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: DWMP capacity planning
official_measurement_examples.fact: Statutory DWMP guidance requires undertakers to assess drainage and sewerage capacity, current and future demand and resilience; a plan-level capacity statement is not a site-specific sewer connection approval.

official_measurement_examples.name: DWMP timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: Second-cycle draft DWMPs are expected by November 2027 and final plans by August 2028, so emerging plan assumptions must remain distinct from current operational capacity.

official_measurement_examples.name: New connection definition
official_measurement_examples.fact: Ofwat defines new connections as access to existing public systems and/or provision of new mains or sewers; the process can involve monopoly companies, self-lay providers or other authorised providers.

official_measurement_examples.name: Connection not capacity guarantee
official_measurement_examples.fact: A request, quote, requisition or self-lay route does not by itself prove available treatment capacity, reinforcement completion, adoption or energisation-equivalent service date.

official_measurement_examples.name: NAV geography distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A NAV changes the appointed provider for a defined service area after Ofwat approval; provider appointment does not itself establish that a particular development has a completed connection.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Water-resource, wastewater and connection processes are utility/regulatory evidence and do not grant land-use planning permission, land ownership or a verified parcel development yield.

core_rules: WRMP is strategic planning not parcel connection offer
future WRMP options are not delivered capacity
regional water plan is not individual site approval
DWMP is strategic drainage/wastewater plan not site connection approval
DWMP plan capacity is not guaranteed treatment headroom for a parcel
connection application is not completed connection
connection quote is not capacity guarantee
self-lay agreement is not adoption completion
NAV appointment is not site connection evidence
water-company service area does not prove title or access rights
utility planning does not grant planning permission
planning permission does not prove water/wastewater capacity
current and emerging plan cycles must remain distinct
reinforcement assumptions must retain timing and delivery status
no parcel utility-capacity clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Environment Agency, Defra, Ofwat and GOV.UK sources checked on 2026-07-26. April-June 2026 water-resource guidance and statutory DWMP/new-connection frameworks were retained with plan/connection/capacity/delivery/planning separation; no parcel promotion.
